summary: Entrance-zone resolution (`doors.resolve_entrance`) is purely geometric — it picks whichever realized zone's rectangle touches the footprint's street wall (`y = footprint.y`), by role priority, with **zero awareness of what the door opens onto beyond that wall** (no check of corridor length, dead ends, or what a visitor passes to reach public rooms). This exact gap was already investigated and explicitly deferred: `docs/L_MASSING_REPRESENTATION_QUALITY_GATE_INVESTIGATION.md` §5.1 reproduces it on the L-parti fixtures and states "not implemented, for its own review." None of C5/C7/C11/C14/C16, `hub_guard`, or `l_massing_guard` would catch a dead-end/pocket next to the entrance — they check reachability, door placeability, corridor *width*, and room-proportion/exposure quality, never corridor *shape* or entrance sequence. The two-column ("deep-primary"/spine) parti is the clearest, always-reproducible case: its `HALL` zone is built as a single unsplit `Leaf` spanning the *entire* footprint depth (`concept_generator.py:2896-2898`), so it always touches the street wall and the front door always opens into literally the end of a full-depth corridor — independently confirmed by `app/demo/contract.py:514-516`'s own comment ("In every spine parti the hall runs the full depth of the house"). Front-band, hub/lobby, and L partis instead route the entrance into a *public room* (not the hall directly) because their hall/lobby sits behind the public band and doesn't front the street — but the L-parti investigation shows this routing has no guarantee of leading toward public rooms rather than past bedrooms (`l_shaped_site_front_arm()` vs `l_shaped_site_deep_primary()` in `geometry_fixtures.py`).
findings: **Q1 — where the hall/corridor's extent is decided.** `doors.resolve_entrance` (`backend/app/vertical_slice/doors.py:147-204`) does NOT decide the corridor's extent — it only picks, among ALREADY-REALIZED room rectangles, whichever one touches the footprint's street wall (`rect.y != footprint.y` filter at `doors.py:175`), by role priority `ENTRANCE_ZONE_PRIORITY = (HALL, CIRCULATION, LIVING, DINING, KITCHEN)` (`doors.py:141-144`). The corridor's actual shape/extent is decided earlier, per-parti, in `concept_generator.py`.

**Two-column / deep-primary spine parti** (`concept_generator.py:2871-2913`, function `_concept_from`): the slicing tree is `Split(Cut.V, west_tree, Split(Cut.V, Leaf("HALL"), east_tree, hall_w), west_w)` (`concept_generator.py:2896-2898`). `HALL` is an un-split `Leaf` under only `Cut.V` (left/right) splits, so its rectangle automatically spans the FULL footprint depth (`fh`) — it always has `rect.y == footprint.y` (street) and `rect.y2 == footprint.y2` (rear wall). This means in this parti the corridor ALWAYS reaches the street wall and the front door ALWAYS opens into the very end of a full-depth corridor. Independently confirmed by `app/demo/contract.py:514-516` comment: "In every spine parti the hall runs the full depth of the house."

**Front-band parti** (`concept_generator.py:2979-2995`, `_front_band_concept`, sized in `_plan_front_band`/`_plan_front_band_at` at `3229-3421`): the hall sits BEHIND the public band and does not touch the street wall at all — explicitly stated in `doors.py:151-156`'s docstring ("THE DEFECT THIS REPLACES") and in `concept_generator.py:2467-2474` (`_build_access` comment): the hall's opening (`hall_public`) borders only the FIRST public zone; every LATER band zone "shares no boundary with it." So in this parti the entrance opens into a PUBLIC room, not the hall, and `resolve_entrance`'s width/leftmost tiebreak (`doors.py:194`) picks whichever public zone fronts the street widest — which is not guaranteed to be the same zone the hall opens into.

**L-parti** (`l_parti.py`): the header diagram (`l_parti.py:1-9`) and comment at `l_parti.py:6` state the hall "spans EXACTLY the seam" between the primary wing and the arm — it is an internal zone, not generally street-facing. `_band_public_order` (`l_parti.py:317-336`, esp. docstring `322-326`) shows the front door's target room depends on `ArmSide`/`ArmEnd` geometry, not on any circulation-awareness: e.g. "stacked at the street (arm at rear), the kitchen is the row next to the hall and the living room fronts the street, so the front door opens into the living room and not the kitchen."

**Hub/lobby parti** (`concept_generator.py:3936-3947`, `_hub_concept`): uses the SAME three-band structure as front-band (lobby is "the middle band's centre leaf"), so it also does not front the street directly. Its docstring explicitly states the team already moved away from a straight corridor here BECAUSE of a measured defect ("a hall spine at long/short 9.4 where every reference [of 21 professional plans] has a compact lobby... none a straight double-loaded corridor") — but this rework only fixed corridor *proportion*, not entrance-sequence quality.

**Q2 — corridor endpoint origin: geometry, not topology.** `resolve_entrance`'s own docstring (`doors.py:158-167`) states the rule directly: "the street wall is the bounding box's y = min line, and a zone fronts it when its own wing reaches that line" — a purely geometric test on the REALIZED rectangles. `concept.py`'s `DesiredAccessTopology` graph (Stage 2) is deliberately INTERIOR-ONLY; `validation.py:366-367` states "the entrance is deliberately not part of that graph — it is resolved at site level." This is corroborated by `docs/L_MASSING_REPRESENTATION_QUALITY_GATE_INVESTIGATION.md:297-299`: "`doors.resolve_entrance` picks the entrance zone by (a) which zone's rectangle touches the street wall, (b) role priority... with zero awareness of which WING that zone sits in, or what a visitor walks past to reach the public rooms."

**Q3 — concrete corpus/fixture contexts (from code + the prior investigation; not independently re-run).** (1) `l_shaped_site_front_arm()` (`geometry_fixtures.py:99-103`) — per the investigation report (`docs/L_MASSING_REPRESENTATION_QUALITY_GATE_INVESTIGATION.md:297-302`), reproduced: entrance opens into HALL, which runs the length of the bedroom arm (MASTER, BEDROOM_1, BATH_1 all in the same street-side band as the hall); LIVING/DINING/KITCHEN sit ~7 m back, reachable only through a 1.4 m corridor sandwiched between bedrooms — public rooms are effectively at the far, non-door end of the corridor. (2) `l_shaped_site_deep_primary()` (`geometry_fixtures.py:113-118`) — same massing family, sibling fixture, contrasting case (report lines 303-306): LIVING fronts the street instead, entrance opens straight into it; nothing in the code currently distinguishes the two on entrance-sequence grounds. (3) The DEFAULT two-column/spine parti (any brief realizing `_concept_from`, `concept_generator.py:2871-2913`, including the frozen canonical demo concept itself — `concept.py:73,93-98`, `ENTRANCE_ZONE_ID = "HALL_MAIN"`, an 8:1-aspect circulation strip): the entrance mechanically opens into the near end of a corridor that runs the FULL depth of the house (see Q1), by construction, on essentially every brief that lands this parti — the single most reproducible instance of 'entrance opens into the end of a corridor,' though this is a straight full-depth corridor rather than a stub/pocket per se. (4) A front-band brief where `resolve_entrance`'s width/leftmost tiebreak (`doors.py:194`) selects a public zone OTHER than the one carrying `hall_public` (`concept_generator.py:2467-2474`): the hall's street-facing end would then have no cased opening cut into the wall of the entered room at all — a wall directly adjacent to/behind the entrance sequence. This is INFERRED from the code paths, not confirmed by running the pipeline; flagged for runtime verification (e.g. sweeping `backend/tests/regression_corpus/corpus.json` for front-band strategies where the widest street-fronting public zone != `hall_public`).

**Q4 — which checks would/would not notice a pocket.** NONE of the cited checks would catch a dead-end corridor stub or wall-in-front-of-door next to the entrance: C5 (`validation.py:270-297`) only checks ZONE-level graph reachability over realized connections — a stub is still part of the same HALL zone/rectangle, so it never shows up as an unreachable zone. C7 (`validation.py:310-315`) only checks door clearance on the shared wall it's placed on. C11 (`validation.py:344-356`) only checks the exterior entrance WALK reaches the building line and avoids parking bays — nothing about what's behind the door. C16 (`validation.py:363-384`) only confirms the door sits literally on the boundary of the zone `resolve_entrance` named — it does not evaluate the corridor's overall shape or path quality. C14 (`validation.py:418-432`, `realized_corridor_width_m` at `validation.py:134`) checks corridor WIDTH against the requested value only, never length or dead-ends. `hub_guard.py:39-98,101-153` compares bedroom/master/safe-room aspect, wet adjacency, and delivered area — explicitly no entrance-sequence term (confirmed by the investigation: "`LQuality`... has no term for it," investigation report line 306-307). `l_massing_guard.py` (`ExposureProportions`, `test_concept_and_site.py:41-61` shows its fields: `worst_wet_aspect`, `two_sided_share`) — same gap. Building-level V-checks (`building_validation.py`): V4/V5 (`186-257`) check multi-level reachability/'core entry and arrival edges face circulation' but operate at the BUILDING-CORE level across levels, not within a single level's entrance-to-corridor geometry. `general_pipeline.py:858` explicitly names this: "Entrance-sequence quality is a separate, un-gated follow-up... and is untouched here."

**Q5 — where a topology rule would naturally live.** Extending `DesiredAccessTopology` (`concept.py`) to include the entrance is a poor fit without an architecture decision: the module's own docstring says it is authored using ONLY frozen Geometry Core types with 'no new domain concepts,' and `validation.py:366-367` states the entrance is DELIBERATELY excluded from that graph (resolved at site level in `doors.py` instead) — this is a load-bearing architectural boundary, not an oversight. The most natural, lowest-risk seam is `doors.resolve_entrance` itself (`doors.py:147-204`), extended with a cheap REALIZED-geometry metric — exactly what the investigation recommends (§5.1, line 309-312): "a cheap metric ('does the wing that fronts the street/entrance contain a PUBLIC-group room, or only PRIVATE/SERVICE ones')" — following the same insertion pattern already proven safe by `hub_guard.py` and `l_massing_guard.py` (a REALIZED-plan comparator inserted after solving, never touching candidate generation/topology). A third option exists and is directly relevant: `app/demo/contract.py`'s `_open_corridor_to_public` (`contract.py:510-576`) is precedent for handling corridor/circulation *visual* adjustments as a CONTRACT-LEVEL POST-PROCESS rather than an engine change — and `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md:63-64` has a standing guardrail: 'Corridor opening (hall↔LDK) is a contract-level post-process (`app/demo/contract.py`), not an engine change.' Any Issue contract for this topic should explicitly decide whether the fix is an engine-level candidate-scoring change (`doors.py`/`hub_guard`-style) or a contract-level post-process, since the codebase has an active precedent AND guardrail for the latter on directly analogous corridor topics.

**Tests that currently pin hall/corridor geometry and must stay green:** `backend/tests/vertical_slice/test_concept_and_site.py:31-36` (asserts `HALL_MAIN` has zero shared edge with `BEDROOM_1` and nonzero with `MASTER` — pins the frozen concept's hall adjacency), `:50-68` (entrance_x derived from `concept.entrance_zone_id`'s realized rect). `backend/tests/test_demo_p0.py:1485-1488` (door position lies within its named room's street-wall span), `:1491-1496` (`test_the_entrance_never_opens_into_a_bedroom_or_a_bathroom` — pins ENTRANCE_ZONE_PRIORITY's role set), `:1499-1504` (`test_the_realization_of_the_entrance_is_checked_not_assumed` — pins C16/C5 both True), `:1507-1513` (entrance walk vs parking). `backend/tests/vertical_slice/test_l_parti.py:130-155,195` (L-wing seam/hall geometry), `:335-343` (C22 on the seam). `backend/tests/vertical_slice/test_concept_generator.py:460-548` (hub lobby door count, hub root->HALL forced cuts). `backend/tests/regression_corpus/test_frozen_regression_corpus.py` + `corpus.json` (432-context frozen regression corpus, zero LLM calls, per `docs/wiki/architecture/knowledge-system.md:41-42`) — any entrance/corridor topology change must be run against this corpus before merge.
recommended_approach: Scope the Issue as a diagnostic-then-decision two-phase contract, mirroring the `l_massing_guard`/`hub_guard` precedent: Phase 1 — reproduce and quantify the defect on `l_shaped_site_front_arm()` and a sweep of `backend/tests/regression_corpus/corpus.json` (measure, for each shown plan, whether the entrance-fronting zone or its immediate neighbours lead toward PUBLIC-group rooms without first passing PRIVATE/SERVICE rooms, and whether the corridor's street-facing end has a real cased opening into the entered room). Phase 2 — implement as a REALIZED-metric check inserted at `doors.resolve_entrance` or immediately after it in `general_pipeline.py` (around line 743-751), following the `hub_guard.py`/`l_massing_guard.py` pattern (compare against realized alternatives already in the candidate pool; never touch `DesiredAccessTopology` or candidate generation). Explicitly resolve, as a stated open question in the contract, whether the fix belongs in the engine (`doors.py`/scoring) or as a contract-level post-process like `_open_corridor_to_public` — the repo has a live guardrail (`docs/PROJECT_STATE.md:63-64`) pointing toward the latter for closely analogous corridor-topology adjustments.
risks: `DesiredAccessTopology` is explicitly scoped as interior-only per `concept.py`'s docstring and `validation.py:366-367`; folding the entrance into it would be a foundational architecture change, not a local fix, and risks breaking the Stage2/Stage4 (concept vs site) separation the codebase relies on.

The L-massing investigation already flagged this exact defect and deliberately did NOT fold it into the (already-implemented) `l_massing_guard.py` fix, warning against mixing root causes (`docs/L_MASSING_REPRESENTATION_QUALITY_GATE_INVESTIGATION.md:313-316`, quoting `docs/ROOM_PROPORTION_REPARTITION_REPORT.md`) — an Issue contract that bundles this with unrelated massing/quality work would repeat a named, already-avoided mistake.

`docs/PROJECT_STATE.md:63-64`'s guardrail on corridor-opening being a contract-level, not engine, concern means an engine-level fix could be the wrong layer without an explicit decision; conversely a contract-level-only fix may not be visible to C5/C16/hub_guard-style validation at all, since those run on the ENGINE'S realized geometry before the demo contract post-process.

No runtime test/tool was available in this investigation; the 'pocket/dead-end' framing in Q3 beyond the two directly-reproduced L-parti fixtures is inferred from code paths (front-band tiebreak mismatch) and needs execution against the corpus to confirm before being cited as fact in the Issue contract.
